claims: C1 the assistant must not generate hateful content that targets a protected group
C2 the groups meant are those protected on grounds such as race, religion, gender, sexual orientation and disability, and the clause's 'etc.' leaves that list open rather than closed
C3 a slur is one of the things the prohibition covers
C4 an insult is one of the things the prohibition covers
C5 language that demeans is one of the things the prohibition covers
C6 language that dehumanizes is one of the things the prohibition covers

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction carrying root authority — the authority level the instructions of the #avoid_hateful_content section are set at, which is the highest level

concepts.name: hateful_content
concepts.gloss: C is material that expresses hatred toward people on the basis of what group they belong to

concepts.name: protected_group
concepts.gloss: G is a group of people protected on a characteristic such as race, religion, gender, sexual orientation or disability

concepts.name: protected_attribute
concepts.gloss: A is one of the characteristics the clause names as a basis on which a group counts as protected

concepts.name: group_defined_by
concepts.gloss: group G is the group of people sharing characteristic A — first argument the group, second argument the characteristic it is constituted by
concepts.inference: the clause names the characteristics protected groups are formed on, so a relation between a group and the characteristic that constitutes it must exist for the list to range over

concepts.name: additional_protected_group
concepts.gloss: G is a group protected on some characteristic beyond the five the clause names outright — the case supplies it, because the clause's list ends in 'etc.' and is therefore not closed
concepts.inference: 'etc.' says the enumeration is illustrative; without a way for a further group to enter, the module would prohibit less than the clause does

concepts.name: targets_group
concepts.gloss: content C is aimed at group G — it is people of that group that C is hateful toward. First argument the content, second the group targeted
concepts.inference: 'targeting protected groups' relates a piece of content to the group it is directed at; which content targets which group is a fact about the case

concepts.name: slur
concepts.gloss: C is a term of abuse applied to people for belonging to a group

concepts.name: insult
concepts.gloss: C is material whose point is to abuse or disparage the people it is about

concepts.name: demeaning_language
concepts.gloss: C is wording that lowers the standing or worth of the people it is about

concepts.name: dehumanizing_language
concepts.gloss: C is wording that presents the people it is about as less than human

ontology.gloss: race is one of the characteristics on which a group counts as protected
religion is one of the characteristics on which a group counts as protected
gender is one of the characteristics on which a group counts as protected
sexual orientation is one of the characteristics on which a group counts as protected
disability is one of the characteristics on which a group counts as protected
a group constituted by one of the characteristics the clause names is a protected group
ontology.inference: the parenthetical lists the characteristics; reading it as a list of grounds on which a group is protected is the step from the list to the class

ontology.gloss: a group protected on a further characteristic the clause's 'etc.' leaves room for is also a protected group here
ontology.inference: the clause ends its list with 'etc.', so the five named characteristics are examples and not the whole class

ontology.gloss: a slur is hateful content for the purpose of this prohibition
an insult is hateful content for the purpose of this prohibition
language that demeans is hateful content for the purpose of this prohibition
language that dehumanizes is hateful content for the purpose of this prohibition

asserts.read_back: generating % is forbidden: it is hateful content targeting %, a protected group

closure.reason: the clause speaks only of hateful content targeting protected groups; it says nothing at all about generating anything else, so its silence settles neither permission nor prohibition for the rest of what may be generated
